purpose: Shared research context for the five coursework topics; source-use observations are not device evidence or blanket lecturer endorsement.

documents.role: Course requirements; original retained outside repository
Example source-use audit; original retained outside repository
Example source-use and feedback audit; original retained outside repository

authority.finding: Personal communications are allowed if actually obtained. When earliest funding is unavailable, estimate required capital using bottom-up/top-down approaches and state the method. Relevant source suggestions include filings, registries, Imperial Library/PitchBook, patents and market-specific payment resources.

The examples combine direct product records with disease/workflow studies, investors, grant programmes, transaction databases, supplier material, provider prices, comparisons and reported interviews. Appearance in an example does not establish approval of every attached claim.
Good coverage is annotated beside Quadsense fundraising and the stakeholder map; its scope should not be extended to every reference or conclusion.
Quadsense has comments requesting citations for paraphrases, less basic information and better paragraph structure. Optomed has a warning about lost embedded references and mark deductions.
authority.provenance: Quadsense_MDE.pdf, physical PDF pages 8-9 and 11-12; Optomed_Aurora_MDE_Report.pdf, physical PDF page 1

authority.finding: Assess how well each question can be answered using fact, background, inference and explicit estimates; retain unknowns. Record source fit and access effort before changing a device access label.
authority.provenance: Synthesis of the specification, example audit and selected source checks; not a lecturer quotation

review_scope: All three specification pages were reviewed. Both examples were rendered and their relevant sections and references inspected using extraction/OCR plus visual checks. Important feedback and selected citation details were checked visually. External checking was selective, as recorded below. Database valuations, interview accounts, all patent legal statuses and all payer conclusions were not independently re-established.

rows.sources: WHO; AAO/NEI and disease organisations; epidemiology and screening/cost papers; ophthalmologist and device-company interviews
rows.use: Describe who lacks screening, the burden and geographic distribution of disease, the old care pathway, and practical barriers to access.
rows.alternative: Use disease-level data and studies of the existing care pathway when exact-brand outcome or cost data are limited. Interview a clinician who knows that pathway.
rows.limit: Disease burden is not device benefit. The example itself says savings could not be reliably quantified. A clinician cannot establish product performance outside their experience.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; no source-specific endorsement identified.

rows.sources: Journal studies; WHO/NHS; company projections; commercial market research; studies of dissatisfaction and painful/revision knee replacement
rows.use: Connect osteoarthritis and knee surgery volumes to the specific unresolved problem: poor outcomes, dissatisfaction and the cost of investigation or revision.
rows.alternative: Use procedure registries, epidemiology and studies of current treatment failures, rather than waiting for a device-specific market report.
rows.limit: Overall knee-surgery market size is not the device-eligible population. Company forecasts and commercial market shares need their methods and denominators checked.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; no source-specific endorsement identified.

rows.sources: EPO and USPTO records; patent classification search; company IP list; trademark records
rows.use: Find candidate patent families, dates, jurisdictions and likely inventors; distinguish technical protection from branding.
rows.alternative: Search the original employer/assignee, inventor names, technical features and predecessor devices when the marketed device name returns little.
rows.limit: The authors explicitly assume pre-launch patents may relate to Aurora. Date overlap and common inventors do not prove claim coverage. Independent-claim analysis is still required by the specification.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; not permission to replace claim analysis with a portfolio count.

rows.sources: Espacenet patent family and publications; UK IPO trademark register; reported developer/inventor history
rows.use: Follow the trial-patella kit family and paraphrase its first independent claim, then connect the invention to the device design and development timeline.
rows.alternative: A patent may be filed under a generic technical title, an inventor or an earlier legal entity rather than the product brand. Follow the family and priority chain.
rows.limit: Read the claims of the exact publication/jurisdiction used. Patent status and claims can differ across family members. A trademark supports a branding claim, not technical exclusivity.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; current patent status and all example legal interpretations were not independently re-audited.

rows.sources: IPO prospectus; PitchBook; Tracxn; Tesi investor portfolio; Halma investor annual report; company annual report; former-board interviews
rows.use: Reconstruct the company funding timeline from several sides of each transaction and explain the remaining gaps in early funding and valuations.
rows.alternative: Search investors, grant funders, university commercialisation offices and accelerators as well as the company. If early financing remains unknown, build a labelled estimate under the specification.
rows.limit: Company finance is not spending on Aurora. The example could not calculate valuations. The investor source records EUR 2 million in 2010; the example chart labels a $2 million entry, so retain original currencies and explain conversions.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed. Opening lecturer note criticises lost embedded references, not the absence of confidential valuations.

rows.sources: PitchBook; FinSMEs announcements; company statement; Mercia investor material; Innovate UK Business Connect; CEO personal communication
rows.use: Combine round size, investors, stated use of proceeds and interview-only development/operating costs to explain the path to market.
rows.alternative: Use an investor announcement to check press coverage; funder case studies can identify grants, incubators, partners and non-cash support. Genuine interviews can fill private details.
rows.limit: Database valuations were not independently verified here. Recent grants and funding may also support Hipsense, a different product. Do not assign all company funding to Quadsense.
rows.lecturer_status: A visible "Good coverage" annotation sits beside the fundraising heading on PDF 7. It is positive section feedback, not approval of each number.

rows.sources: Exact FDA 510(k); GUDID and EUDAMED; government guidance; commercial regulatory explainers; prospectus; manufacturer website/certificates; device-company interview
rows.use: Connect the device to its intended use, market pathway, classification, tested standards and manufacturing arrangements.
rows.alternative: Use the regulator decision/summary and instructions for use if the company website is vague; use a prospectus or counterparty record for outsourcing details.
rows.limit: A generic rule does not prove the device complied with it. A supplier capability page does not prove a customer relationship; the prospectus provides the relationship evidence in this example.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; no blanket approval of the example regulatory wording or commercial explainers.

rows.sources: Company launch announcement; FDA classification and exact 510(k) summaries; predicate brochure; MHRA registry; GOV.UK approved-body list; Medsafe guidance; IFU; research papers; supplier sites
rows.use: Explain the original clearance and later version, compare relevant devices, and identify standards and manufacturing tasks.
rows.alternative: The predicate decision and device IFU can explain the evidence route even when detailed development files are unavailable; official registers identify actors and dates.
rows.limit: A predicate brochure is supporting context, not the clearance decision. Registration is not approval. Supplier websites establish capability unless a separate source links them to the exact product.
rows.lecturer_status: Visible comments include "Include citation for paraphrasing" and "Basic Info not needed". These favour precise case evidence over a generic regulation tutorial.

rows.sources: Company/distributor price pages; a manufacturer blog listing CPT amounts; newer product pages; NCQA HEDIS; reported interviews; a stakeholder map
rows.use: Separate hospital purchase or subscription from the payment for screening, and discuss workflow, access and possible economic incentives.
rows.alternative: Use a clearly labelled successor/comparator price to make a range; study the service payment and procurement route rather than searching only for a brand-specific code.
rows.limit: Aurora IQ pricing is a proxy, not verified original-Aurora pricing. Reference [97] does contain tariff amounts, but is a manufacturer blog dated 2021, not a current payer rate table. A newer AI product cannot automatically establish the original device workflow or savings.
rows.lecturer_status: Source use observed; no visible positive annotation specifically validating these proxy or tariff claims.

rows.sources: CMS; NHS OPCS; New Zealand coding/device purchasing resources; private-provider surgery prices; NHS recovery information; company FAQ; CEO personal communication
rows.use: Map who buys the sensor, how it fits within surgery, what costs might change and where benefits and money flow.
rows.alternative: Use procedure-level payment, hospital procurement and a transparent scenario model when a distinct device payment code or long-term economic study is absent.
rows.limit: The example says true economic impact remains predictive. No separate device code does not establish lack of payment. A private surgery charge is not an NHS cost or tariff; the CMS homepage alone cannot establish a coverage conclusion.
rows.lecturer_status: "Good coverage" appears beside the stakeholder map on PDF 13; "Poor paragraph structure" appears on PDF 12. Do not extend the map praise to every reimbursement claim.

external_checks.finding: The associate-investment discussion records EUR 2 million invested in Optomed in December 2010.
external_checks.limit: Direct evidence of a company investment, not Aurora R&D spend. The example chart labels a $2 million entry; retain original currency and explain conversions.
external_checks.coverage: Targeted associate-investment passage, printed page 41; not the entire report

external_checks.limit: Confirms a round beyond secondary funding news. It does not independently establish PitchBook pre/post valuations or exact device development spend.

external_checks.source_title: Innovate UK Business Connect: Eventum growth case study, 2 June 2025

external_checks.limit: Useful company development/support evidence. Do not assign all grants to original Quadsense development.

external_checks.source_title: Optomed: diabetic retinopathy prevention blog, 2 March 2021
external_checks.finding: The recovered target for Optomed reference [97] contains CPT 92250 and a reimbursement range.
external_checks.limit: The figures are present, but a manufacturer blog from 2021 does not establish the current payer rate, eligibility, place or configuration.

external_checks.title: Bundled service payment
external_checks.source_title: CMS: Medicare Payment Systems, outpatient packaged costs
external_checks.finding: CMS explains that some integral items and services are included in the main outpatient hospital payment.
external_checks.limit: Supports investigation of procedure-level payment when a separate device payment is absent; does not establish Quadsense coverage.

external_checks.limit: Useful for pilot/accelerator context, not IPO share figures or an automatic Aurora-specific result. Figure 8's separate reference [46] requires its own check.
